subject: Per-token ladder: fallback buckets + margin-stack construct
messages:
From: Lydia Chang <lydia.chang@fasthealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@fasthealth.com
Date: 2028-03-22 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify per-token tiers + fallback behavior

Hi Grace,

Quick question as we prepare the SOW: our procurement team is seeing two different constructs in your pricing worksheet — a blended-rate ladder and what you call a 'margin-stack' (marginal tiers with a fallback). We need one clear picture for legal: will FastHealth be billed at a blended effective rate for the month, or at marginal rates by breakpoint with a fallback to the next available model if hosted capacity is constrained?

Use case details: we expect a steady 350M tokens/mo baseline with 10M-40M bursts on certain campaign days. We care about predictable $/token on the baseline and graceful behavior during bursts.

Can you send a short summary and the operational guarantees (true-up mechanics, clawback, and where the fallback kicks in)? Also please attach the final SOW version.

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Chang
Head of Procurement, FastHealth

--

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_occonnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chang <lydia.chang@fasthealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-22 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify per-token tiers + fallback behavior

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear ask. Short version up front: we can support marginal-tier billing (per-breakpoint marginal pricing) with an explicit fallback policy; we do not automatically convert to a blended monthly rate unless you request a blended invoice in your contract. Below is the operational summary and where we put guardrails. I'm attaching an annotated SOW and a 1-page playbook.

What we propose (summary):
- Billing model: marginal per-token tiers (you pay the marginal $/token for tokens inside each band).
- Fallback buckets: when your committed model or tier is unavailable (e.g., capacity or region outage), requests fall back to a compatible lower-cost model variant with known quality delta. Fallback is opt-in per route and modeled in the SOW (see section 3.4).
- Predictability: we offer a 'sustainment credit' for baseline shortfalls/excesses — any variance inside a 15% monthly corridor auto-true-ups at the next billing cycle; larger deltas trigger the scheduled true-up clause.
- Clawbacks & credits: if fallback serves >10% of tokens in a given month (across a route), you receive a service credit tied to latency/availability SLO misses per the SLA.

Operational triggers (where fallback kicks in):
1) Active model/instance pool < 75% of target throughput for 3+ consecutive minutes.
2) Regional capacity >= 120s expected queue for the route for 2 minutes.
3) Manual failover during maintenance windows (documented in calendar).

Attachments: FastHealth_SOW_v2.pdf, fallback-rate-playbook.pdf, commit_breakpoints.xlsx

Next steps I recommend:
1) I can send a worked example for your baseline 350M token shape showing month-end blended vs marginal invoices (two columns) so procurement can evaluate cashflow.
2) If procurement prefers blended invoicing, we'll include a blended reconciliation clause (we can compute an effective monthly blended rate for billing only, while keeping per-token marginal math in the background for platform routing).

Happy to hop on a short call with your procurement/legal and Ben (pricing lead) to walk through the SOW language. Proposed times: Tue/Wed this week 10–11am PT.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0118

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-23 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarify per-token tiers + fallback behavior — internal: concession guidance

Ben / Aisha — forwarding Lydia's ask and my response. Two items I want quick guidance on before I lock the final wording:

1) Margin-stack vs blended: Lydia's team prefers a predictable invoice. Procurement will push hard for a blended monthly cap if the effective blended rate is <= their target. We should be ready with a blended-invoicing option but charge a 3% administrative fee for blended reconciliation work (covers accounting). Thoughts?

2) Fallback credit threshold: I suggested a 10% threshold for credits. Sales ops historically pushes for 15% to avoid small credit churn. Given FastHealth's baseline is 350M tokens, 10% is material but also represents real user impact visibility. Recommend we keep 10% for enterprise deals with an option to escalate to 15% for pilot/POC. Approve?

3) Burst behavior: they have 10–40M burst days. Should we offer a short-term burst buffer (one-time 25M free burst in month 1) to reduce friction on signing?

Proposed concession policy (my ask): blended-invoice option (opt-in) + 3% admin fee; fallback credit at 10% threshold for Enterprise; one-time 25M burst buffer for month 1. If approved, I'll update the SOW and send final to Lydia.

—Grace

Subject: Updated proposal: margin-stack + blended-invoice option (SOW v2 attached)

Hi Lydia — following up with the updated, clearer proposal and the attached annotated SOW (v2). I incorporated our internal approvals and the concession we discussed. Key points: 

- Default billing: marginal per-token ladder (you'll see exact tier math in the attached commit_breakpoints.xlsx).
- Blended invoice option: available on request. If you choose blended billing, Redwood will compute a monthly effective blended $/token for invoicing; the platform will still enforce marginal routing for serving. Blended invoicing includes a 3% administrative fee to cover reconciliation and reporting.
- Fallback policy: opt-in per route. If fallback serves >10% of tokens in a month, FastHealth receives a credit against next invoice per SLA table (see SLO credits table in SOW).
- One-time onboarding burst buffer: a single, non-recurring 25M token buffer in month one to smooth go-live bursts.
- True-up mechanics: variances inside a 15% corridor auto-true-up to the committed tier at month-end; overage/shortfall outside corridor trigger the true-up schedule in section 5.2.

I've attached a short worked example comparing marginal billing vs blended invoice for your 350M baseline + 25M burst month — see tab "WorkedExample" in commit_breakpoints.xlsx. If you prefer, Ben can join a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through the math.

If the above looks good, please confirm and we'll finalize SOW signatures.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
